items.name: MapReduce
items.explanation: A way to process a huge dataset in large batches: many machines each handle a slice, then the results are combined. Every step finishes over the whole dataset before the next begins.

assumedBy.quote: The MapReduces must be run again over the entire repository, that is, over both the new pages and the old pages.

items.name: Bigtable
items.explanation: Google's distributed storage system for structured data. It scales to huge tables but does not give programmers multi-row transactions, which Percolator adds on top.

assumedBy.quote: Distributed storage systems like Bigtable [9] can scale to the size of our repository

sources.title: Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data

items.name: Isolation levels and SERIALIZABLE
items.explanation: An isolation level says how much concurrent transactions can see of each other. Serializable is the strictest: the result is as if they ran one at a time.

assumedBy.quote: In fact, CockroachDB provides the strongest level of isolation, SERIALIZABLE, so that the integrity of your data is always preserved.

items.name: RocksDB
items.explanation: An embedded key-value database that a program links in and uses as its storage engine. It writes bytes to disk so committed data survives a restart.

assumedBy.quote: CockroachDB uses RocksDB, an embedded key-value database maintained by Facebook, as its storage engine.
